THIRD EXECUTABLE DOCS RECEIPT — REPRESENT A RECALL. This is workflow 2 in the
accepted six-workflow spine, executed by codex-storymodel-collab against exact
exported main e584ad6d8a1b6bc5cb28ac1c406a239114f1f48a. No repository path was
edited.

The example deliberately continues with the same public precise War of the
Ghosts recall fixture used by the alignment guide. It stops before source
alignment so a reader can see that recall structure is its own object.

SOURCE SHA-256:
10a8749109d4bce9679e81f7f2c882e5d2272c53297e1819f88ea4467563bf9c

```scala
package docsprobe

import storymodel4s.core.StorySource
import storymodel4s.fixtures.wog.WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.*
import storymodel4s.recall.RecallSegmenter

/** Public-API-only tour of a structured recall graph. */
@main def representARecall(): Unit =
  val paraphrase = recallParaphrases.find(_.kind == ParaphraseKind.Precise).getOrElse {
    throw new IllegalStateException("the public precise-recall fixture is missing")
  }
  val transcript = StorySource
    .fromText(paraphrase.text, Some("War of the Ghosts recall"))
    .fold(error => throw new IllegalArgumentException(error.message), identity)
  val recall = RecallSegmenter.segment(transcript)

  println(s"transcript: ${transcript.canonicalText}")
  println(s"recall units: ${recall.units.size}")
  println(s"implicit recall-order links: ${recall.chain.size}")
  println(
    s"explicit recall relations: ${recall.relations.temporal.size} temporal, " +
      s"${recall.relations.causal.size} causal, " +
      s"${recall.relations.coreference.size} coreference"
  )
  println(s"recall-side entities: ${recall.relations.entities.size}")
  println()

  recall.ordered.foreach { unit =>
    val proposition = unit.proposition
    val participants = proposition.participants
      .map(participant => s"${participant.role}=${participant.label}")
      .mkString(", ")
    println(s"unit ${unit.ordinal}: ${unit.text}")
    println(s"  discourse function: ${unit.function}")
    println(s"  expressed uncertainty: ${unit.expressedUncertainty}")
    println(
      s"  proposition: ${proposition.predicate.getOrElse("unknown")}; " +
        s"polarity=${proposition.polarity}; modality=${proposition.modality}"
    )
    println(s"  participants: $participants")
  }

  recall.relations.temporal.foreach { edge =>
    println(
      s"temporal: unit ${recall.byId(edge.from).ordinal} " +
        s"${edge.relation} unit ${recall.byId(edge.to).ordinal}"
    )
  }
  recall.relations.coreference.foreach { link =>
    val anaphor = link.anaphor.slice(transcript.canonicalText).getOrElse("?")
    val antecedent =
      recall.relations.entities.find(_.id == link.antecedent).map(_.label).getOrElse("?")
    println(s"coreference: $anaphor -> $antecedent (${link.kind})")
  }
```

EXACT COMMAND SHAPE:

```sh
sbt -Dstorymodel4s.grakern.build=/absolute/path/to/pinned-grakern \
  "fixturesJVM/runMain docsprobe.representARecall"
```

RUN_EXIT=0. Captured output SHA-256:
87538cf53ad817aaea3bda0cd32e5a9a3843ffff39aaba00512824bcd5a8128b

```text
transcript: One of the men with him got hit by an arrow and they lifted him into the boat.
recall units: 2
implicit recall-order links: 1
explicit recall relations: 0 temporal, 0 causal, 1 coreference
recall-side entities: 1

unit 0: One of the men with him got hit by an arrow
  discourse function: EpisodicAssertion
  expressed uncertainty: Unmarked
  proposition: get; polarity=Positive; modality=Asserted
  participants: Agent=men
unit 1: they lifted him into the boat.
  discourse function: EpisodicAssertion
  expressed uncertainty: Unmarked
  proposition: lift; polarity=Positive; modality=Asserted
  participants: Agent=they, Patient=him
coreference: they -> men (Pronoun)
```

INTERPRETATION: the recall transcript becomes two ordered idea units, each with
its own discourse function, expressed-uncertainty feature, shallow proposition,
polarity, modality, and recall-named participants. Recall order is implicit in
the ordinals and available as one chain link; explicit temporal and causal
relations are separate typed layers. The coreference layer resolves plural
"they" backward to "men".

LIMITS THAT THE PAGE SHOULD TEACH, NOT HIDE: RecallSegmenter is the documented
deterministic rule-based baseline, not a scientific claim about recall language.
Its sketch normalizes "got hit" to predicate get and does not recover every
semantic role. It does not link singular "him" to the only plural antecedent,
which is the correct fail-closed number behavior even though the resulting
reference remains unresolved. The recall graph carries no source anchor yet;
partial source/external alignment is the next workflow, not a field silently
filled by segmentation.

The exact formatted source reran with RUN_EXIT=0 and scalafmtCheckAll then
passed. The run used Homebrew Java 25.0.1, so it is not JDK 17/21 compatibility
evidence. No automatic acquisition or alignment-quality claim follows.
